entities.summary: Juan de Álava (1480-1537) was a Spanish architect renowned for his distinctive stonework in the Plateresque style, which dominated architectural design in the Iberian Peninsula during the late 16th century. Born in Zigoitia, Álava, Spain, Juan de Álava was the son of a local lord and received a humanist education in Salamanca, where he developed a passion for classical Greek and Roman architecture. His most notable works include the Church of San Martín in Larrabetzu, Navarre, and the Convent of San Francisco in Tafalla, Navarre, which showcased his innovative use of stone and ornate details. Álava's designs not only reflected the artistic and cultural currents of the time but also had a lasting impact on the development of Spanish architecture. His legacy extends to the present day, with his work influencing generations of architects and designers. In the words of art historian Juan de Villalta y de las Posadas, 'Juan de Álava was a master of the Plateresque style, whose works are a testament to the grandeur and beauty of Spanish architecture.' The Spanish monarchs, Charles V and Philip II, were among Álava's patrons, recognizing the value of his innovative designs and commissioning him to create numerous projects throughout the kingdom. Álava's contributions to Spanish architecture not only enriched the cultural heritage of the Iberian Peninsula but also paved the way for future generations of architects and designers. His influence can be seen in the works of later architects, such as Juan Goytisolo, who was inspired by Álava's use of stone and ornate details. In conclusion, Juan de Álava's remarkable career as a Spanish architect left an indelible mark on the history of architecture, cementing his place as one of the most important figures in the development of Spanish architecture.
